**Critical Flaws:**
Despite the strong empirical performance, the evaluation contains a **major structural confounding variable**: the location encoder for FS-SINR is fine-tuned, whereas the baselines (SINR, LE-SINR) use a frozen encoder, with only the classification head trained at inference. The authors explicitly state this difference but fail to provide an ablation study isolating the effect of the encoder fine-tuning. Since deep neural networks are highly sensitive to initialization and fine-tuning strategies, it is impossible to attribute the 5–10% improvement (Figure 3) to the proposed "few-shot embedding" mechanism versus the mere advantage of end-to-end fine-tuning versus training just a logistic regression head. Without this ablation, the central claim of the paper (that the architecture itself enables few-shot success without per-species training) is not proven.

**Minor Issues:**
The comparison to the zero-shot baseline LD-SDM is missing actual numbers, relying on a variant instead of a direct comparison. The lack of significance testing with only 3 random seeds further weakens the statistical rigor.
